annotations.text:
CLICK IT — the whole pipeline works.

Rail: every entry moves you. Uploading stays amber from anywhere while a run is blocked.

Uploading: answer the question and it advances — group → lossy master → metadata → fill a request → result. The strip under the header fills in as you go. "Start over" resets it.

Queue: tick rows, press Download — they move to Downloading and the rail counts change.

Requests: press Check repeatedly to watch the bar advance a row at a time.

DRY RUN in the header toggles. Live changes the result wording.

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY

Palette: warm near-black instead of #16161d, one amber that only ever means "this needs you", green only for "there is something to upload here". No violet, no 10px pills, no gradient anywhere.

Type: IBM Plex Sans, with Plex Mono for everything you compare across rows — budgets, paths, counts, track numbers. Numbers line up because they are tabular.

Density: rules instead of cards. The queue shows twice as many rows in the same space, and a row carries its per-tracker state instead of one merged line.

Metadata form: the hint sits under its own field, so a long one can never push its input out of line with the rest of the row.

WHAT THIS PROTOTYPE DOES NOT COVER YET

Browse and Scan land on Settings — I have not drawn them.

Settings is one screen of groups, not the real form. It shows the regrouping (by what you are doing, not by config section) and nothing else.

The numbers are sample values shaped like your real ones, so the layout is honest about the widths it has to hold. None of it is live data.

Say which of these you want next and I will draw it before touching app.css.

Not chosen — kept for reference.

B was the furthest from an AI-built app but the least dense; C was the smallest leap but still a dark app with cards and rounded corners.

Delete this page whenever you want.
